publications.title: Judgment Aggregation in Creative Production: Evidence from the Movie Industry
publications.description: We study a novel, low-cost approach to aggregating judgment from a large number of industry experts on ideas that they encounter in their normal course of business. Our context is the movie industry, in which customer appeal is difficult to predict and investment costs are high. The Black List, an annual publication, ranks unproduced scripts based on anonymous nominations from film executives. This approach entails an inherent trade-off: Low participation costs enable high response rates, but nominations lack standard criteria, and which voters see which ideas is unobservable and influenced by various factors. Despite these challenges, we find that such aggregation is predictive: Listed scripts are substantially more likely to be released than observably similar, but unlisted, scripts, and, conditional on release and investment levels, listed scripts generate higher box-office revenues. We also find that this method mitigates entry barriers for less-experienced writers, as (i) their scripts are more likely to be listed than those by experienced writers and to rank higher if listed and (ii) within scripts by less-experienced writers, being listed is associated with a higher release rate. Yet, the gap in release probabilities relative to experienced writers remains large, even for top-ranked scripts. These results can be explained by the premise that scripts from less-experienced writers are more visible among eligible voters than scripts from experienced writers. This highlights idea visibility as an important determinant of votes and surfaces the trade-offs, as well as potential limitations, associated with such methods.

publications.title: Death of the Salesman but Not the Sales Force: How Interested Promotion Skews Scientific Valuation
publications.publishedAt: The American Journal of Sociology · Oct 1, 2019
publications.description: Whereas research has demonstrated how social cues appearing as disinterested social validation can skew valuation processes, interested promotion may be at least as important. This factor is examined here via the premature death of 720 elite life scientists. Especially when scientists are young and their articles have received little attention, their deaths stimulate a long-lasting, positive increase in citation rates, relative to trajectories for equivalent articles authored by counterfactual (i.e., still-living) scientists. These patterns seem largely explained by a spike in posthumous recognition efforts by the deceased scientists’ associates. The upshot is clear evidence of informational inefficiency, which derives from the challenges of absorbing the massive volume of research produced by the scientific community and from its ambivalence about the norm of disinterestedness.

As my senior design project, my group and I worked closely with frying oil science. In this project, we worked to create a process, which would maintain the percentage of free fatty acid in frying oil at a specified minimum. 
Free fatty acids (FFAs) generate from the hydrolysis of triglycerides, meaning that when the oil comes in contact with water, it generates these molecules. When frying  potato chips, the water inside the potatoes interacts with the triglycerides in the frying oil to generate FFAs. This reaction is further sped up at high frying temperatures. 
For this project, a process was developed that removed FFAs from oil by liquid-liquid extraction, where the solvent used for extraction was an ethanol-water mixture. This process was optimized to remove a maximum amount of FFAs, while also maintaining the frying oil's properties intact so that it can be safely consumed. 
A simplified version of this process can be seen in the uploaded media.

about:
My name is Dr. Mathieu Davis, and I am a graduate of the Harvard Business School (HBS) where I served as Vice President of Alumni for the African American Student Union (AASU) and as participant in HBS's Impact Investment Fund. During business school, I was a philanthropic investor through the Harbus Education Fund, where I performed due diligence (financial and social impact) and selected organizations to receive grants of up to $50k. Additionally, I served as a member of the Impact Investing Club and Black Investing Club and as a reviewer for AASU's annual Black New Venture Competition. I am also the co-founder of Davesi Investments, LLC, a real estate investment company that assesses and analyzes opportunities in the Philadelphia market with the potential to generate at least 20% ROI. As a founder, I manage a team of contractors, architects, and real estate agents, to renovate and develop modern homes.

Before joining HBS, I was a published researcher with expertise in biomechanics, including orthopedics, gait kinematics, footwear performance, automobile product liability, and motor vehicle occupant safety and risk. In addition, I have a strong engineering and scientific background with a Ph.D. in mechanical engineering from the University of Michigan. After finishing my Ph.D., I completed a year in South Africa as a Fulbright Fellow, where I researched knee arthroplasty and gait biomechanics at Stellenbosch University. While in South Africa, I participated in and led several community engagement projects with the local youth. The most meaningful of these was developing and implementing a LEGO Mindstorms after-school outreach program for the Biomedical Engineering Research Group. Throughout my career, I have emphasized giving back to my community through various volunteering and mentorship endeavors. For example, while working at Exponent as an engineering consultant for six years, I founded and chaired a DEI initiative for consultants and staff. I also served on the company's first DEI Advisory committee to the Chief Executive Officer. 

I founded the OMEGA Promise Foundation three years ago, a non-profit mentorship organization geared towards serving underrepresented minorities from K-12 and beyond. I continue to work tirelessly in my community to help at-risk youth and strive to be a more informed and outspoken advocate for the voiceless.

publications.title: Incidence and Mechanisms of Head, Cervical Spine, Lumbar Spine, and Lower Extremity Injuries for Occupants in Low- to Moderate-Speed Rear-End Collisions
publications.description: Automotive accidents and subsequent personal injury claims incur substantial costs annually. While seat and head restraint design continue to evolve and improve, occupant safety and injury risk assessment in rear-end collisions remain at the forefront of automotive innovation. In this study, we combined statistical analyses of nine years (2007-2015) of data from the National Automotive Sampling System Crashworthiness Data System (NASS-CDS) database and one year (2017) of data from the Crash Investigation Sampling System (CISS) database with data acquired from vehicle-to-vehicle crash tests conducted with instrumented anthropomorphic test device (ATD) occupants. Together, these analyses were used to compare and relate field injury rates with potential mechanisms underlying head, cervical spine, lumbar spine, and lower extremity injuries in low-to moderate-speed rear-end collisions. First, we performed statistical analyses of the NASS-CDS and CISS databases to estimate the rate of AIS 2+ and AIS 3+ cervical spine, lumbar spine, and lower extremity injuries, as well as a subset of AIS 2+ and AIS 3+ internal head injuries, including recorded unconsciousness and concussion. The results of these analyses were then compared to measured occupant loading data from rear-end crash tests performed at delta-Vs ranging from 5.6 to 19.5 km/h, using restrained, nominally positioned, and instrumented Hybrid III 50th percentile male ATDs. Kinematic and kinetic data for the head, cervical spine, lumbar spine, and lower extremities collected in the low- to moderate-speed rear-end crash tests were well below injury thresholds. Analysis of the NASS-CDS and CISS databases demonstrated low rates of injury to the head, cervical spine, lumbar spine, and lower extremities in low- to moderate-speed rear-end collisions. Review of these rear-end crashes revealed that, potential muscle activation, occupant age, and occupant compartment configuration may play a role in injury likelihood.

publications.title: Incidence and Mechanism of Head, Cervical Spine, Lumbar Spine, and Lower Extremity Injuries for Occupants in Low- to Moderate-Speed Frontal Collisions
publications.description: Automotive accidents and subsequent personal injury claims incur substantial costs annually. While three-point restraint usage, dual-stage airbags, and knee bolster and side curtain airbags have become more ubiquitous and, in some cases, governmentally mandated for front seat occupants, occupant safety and injury risk assessment continue to be at the forefront of automotive innovation. In this study, we combined analyses of the National Automotive Sampling System Crashworthiness Data System (NASS-CDS; 2007-2015) and the Crash Investigation Sampling System (CISS; 2017) with data acquired from vehicle-to-vehicle crash tests conducted with instrumented anthropomorphic test device (ATD) occupants. Together, these analyses were used to compare and relate field injury rates with potential injury mechanisms in low- to moderate-speed frontal collisions. First, low- to moderate-speed (delta-V ≤ 24 km/h) frontal crash data from NASS-CDS and CISS were analyzed to estimate the rate of AIS 2+ and AIS 3+ cervical spine, lumbar spine, and lower extremity injuries, as well as a subset of AIS 2+ and 3+ head injuries including recorded unconsciousness and concussion. The results of these analyses were related to occupant loading data from comparative frontal crash tests, conducted at delta-Vs ranging from 6 to 19 km/h. Kinematic and kinetic data for the head, cervical spine, lumbar spine, and femur collected in the frontal crash tests were well below injury thresholds. Analysis of the NASS-CDS and CISS data demonstrated low rates of injury to the head, cervical spine, lumbar spine, and lower extremities in low- to moderate-speed frontal collisions. Review of these frontal crashes revealed that several factors, outside of collision severity, may affect injury likelihood, including muscle activation, seatbelt status, frontal and knee bolster airbag deployment, seat track position, out-of-positioning, age, gender, and interaction with vehicle interior structures.

publications.title: Evaluation of Occupant Kinematics during Low- to Moderate-Speed Side Impacts
publications.description:
While nearly 50 percent of occupants in side-impact
collisions are in vehicles that experience a velocity
change (delta-V) below 15.0 kph (9.3 mph), full
scale crash testing research at these delta-Vs is limited.
Understanding occupant kinematics in response to these types
of side impacts can be important to the design of side-impact
safety countermeasures, as well as for evaluating potential
interactions with interior vehicle structures and/or with other
occupants in the vehicle. In the current study, two full-scale
crash tests were performed utilizing a late-model, mid-size
sedan with disabled airbags. The test vehicle was impacted by
a non-deformable moving barrier on the driver side at an
impact speed of 10.0 kph (6.2 mph) in the first test and then on
the passenger side at an impact speed of 21.6 kph (13.4 mph)
in the second test, resulting in vehicle lateral delta-Vs of 6.1 kph
(3.8 mph) and 14.0 kph (8.7 mph), respectively. As can occur
in real-world collisions, the initial impacts to the vehicle were
followed by subsequent lower severity contacts. In both tests,
Hybrid III 50th percentile male anthropomorphic test devices
(ATDs) were restrained in the driver and right front passenger
seats. The current study allowed for comparison of the nearand
far-side occupant kinematics during the multiple vehicle
contacts. The occupant kinematics were evaluated using highspeed
video recordings of the collisions. Motion tracking was
used to evaluate excursion magnitudes and excursion velocities
during these collisions and demonstrated that, in general, the
magnitudes of occupant excursion and velocity were greater
in the higher-speed collision than in the lower-speed collision.
Occupant motions relative to vehicle structures and relative to
the other occupant were evaluated. In general, the kinematics
included oscillatory responses of the ATDs following the initial
motion toward the impact and return motion toward and
beyond the original seated position.

publications.title: Thoracic spine extension injuries in occupants with pre-existing conditions during rear end collisions.
publications.description: Certain ankylosing spondyloarthropathies such as ankylosing spondylitis (AS) or diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) can substantially alter clinicopathologic spine biomechanics as well as injury mechanisms in rear-end motor vehicle collisions. AS is an inflammatory disease which can lead to structural impairments of the spine secondary to flowing ossification along the spinal column, including ossification across the spinal discs, facet joints, and ligaments, and it has also been associated with diffuse osteoporosis of the spine. DISH is characterized by excess bone formation along the spinal column, encompassing the annulus and forming the thickest and strongest bridging osteophytes over adjacent vertebral bodies at the level of the disc space. In both conditions the spine is mechanically stiffened and generally more kyphotic than a healthy spine. This paper presents a series of case studies in which a front-seat occupant with ankylosing spondyloarthropathy experienced a moderate- or high-speed rear-end collision and sustained a thoracic spine fracture/dislocation, often with spinal cord injuries. Forward acceleration of the occupant by the seat back in each case resulted in straightening of the kyphotic thoracic spine and consequent extension fractures of the pathologically stiff and brittle thoracic spine. This paper illustrates the predisposition of thoracic fracture for this segment of the population with spinal pathologies such as DISH and AS in rear impacts and notes the role that seat back stiffness could play in injury mechanism for these individuals.

publications.title: Evaluation of occupant loading in low- to moderate-speed frontal and rear-end motor vehicle collisions
publications.description: Low- to moderate-speed motor vehicle collisions are common roadway occurrences that are generally associated with low rates of reported injury. While such complaints are generally infrequent, claims of injuries resulting from low- to moderate-speed motor vehicle collisions persist. A limited body of literature using quantitative techniques and full-scale crash tests is available to assess the injury potential associated with such collisions. Prior studies have analyzed occupant kinematics and kinetics as well as human injury risk in low- to moderate-speed collisions with older vehicle vintages but do not assess the effects of updated vehicle interior designs and occupant protection devices reflective of efforts to optimize occupant kinematics and reduce occupant loading and injury risk in more modern vehicles. This study was conducted to evaluate the injury potential for occupants of vehicles with modern design elements involved in low- to moderate-speed inline motor vehicle collisions. We expected to find that occupants in modern vehicles would demonstrate low potential for injury in such collisions.

publications.title: Increased susceptibility to microdamage in Brtl/+ mouse model for osteogenesis imperfecta.
publications.description: Results show that Brtl/+ ulnae subject to normal cage activity demonstrate an inherently larger amount of microdamage than WT controls. Following axial compressive loading, Brtl/+ ulnae are more prone to damage than WT counterparts despite demonstrating a greater resistance to whole-bone deformation. Fracture toughness results demonstrate that Brtl/+ specimens display lower fracture toughness values than their WT counterparts. Correlations show that microdamage levels tend to increase as fracture toughness decreases. Together, these findings may have strong clinical implications for explaining increased fragility and remodeling activity in OI patients.

headline: Project Leader at Boston Consulting Group (BCG)
about:
I am currently a project leader at BCG primarily working in Healthcare.  Before entering into consulting, I studied Comparative Biomechanics at Temple University, where I received my Ph.D. in Biology and M.S. in Exercise Physiology. 

My work examined stabilization techniques in lizard locomotion over complex terrain including obstacles and granular media using a combination of experimental work and robotics. My research interests included the maintenance of stability while navigating perturbations, kinematic and kinetic adaptations of organisms and robots in unfamiliar and novel environments, and methods for the quantification of stability for comparative purposes across conditions, species, and for widespread and readily implemented experimental use.

publications.title: Engineered Tumor-Targeted T Cells Mediate Enhanced Anti-Tumor Efficacy Both Directly and through Activation of the Endogenous Immune System
publications.description:
Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has proven clinically beneficial against B cell acute
lymphoblastic leukemia and non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. However, suboptimal clinical outcomes
have been associated with decreased expansion and persistence of adoptively transferred CAR
T cells, antigen-negative relapses, and impairment by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment.
Improvements in CAR T cell design are required to enhance clinical efficacy, as well as broaden the
applicability of this technology. Here, we demonstrate that interleukin-18 (IL-18)-secreting CAR
T cells exhibit enhanced in vivo expansion and persistence and significantly increase long-term survival in syngeneic mouse models of both hematological and solid malignancies. In addition, we demonstrate that IL-18-secreting CAR T cells are capable of modulating the tumor microenvironment, as well
as enhancing an effective endogenous anti-tumor immune response. IL-18-secreting CAR T cells represent a promising strategy to enhance the clinical outcomes of adoptive T cell therapy.

publications.title: IL-18 Secreting CAR T Cells Enhance Cell Persistence, Induce Prolonged B Cell Aplasia and Eradicate CD19+ Tumor Cells without Need for Prior Conditioning
publications.description:
Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has consistently shown significant results against acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) in clinical trials1. However, results with other hematological or solid malignancies have been far more modest2. These disparate outcomes could be partially due to an inhibitory tumor microenvironment that suppresses CAR T cell function3. Thus, in order to expand the anti-tumor CAR T cell applications, a novel strategy in which these cells are capable of overcoming the hostile tumor microenvironment is needed.

The cytokine interleukin-18 (IL-18) induces IFN-γ secretion, enhances the Th1 immune response and activates natural killer and cytotoxic T cells4. Early phase clinical trials that utilized systemic administration of recombinant IL-18 for the treatment of both solid and hematological malignancies have demonstrated the safety of this therapy5.

We hypothesize that CAR T cells that constitutively secrete IL-18 could enhance CAR T cell survival and anti-tumor activity, and also activate cells from the endogenous immune system.

publications.title: STAT3 Activation Is Preceded By Two Independent Pathways (BCR-BTK and IL6-JAK) in Mantle Cell Lymphoma
publications.description:
To increase the possibility of therapeutic potential in mantle cell lymphoma patients treated with the BTK inhibitor, Ibrutinib, the investigation of BTK-dependent/independent signaling pathways is needed. Using both established MCL cell lines and primary MCL cells as a model system, our data demonstrated that ibrutinib effectively inhibited BTK phosphorylation along with quick STAT3 inactivation within 30 minutes of ibrutinib incubation at a dose lower than 100nM. Since the results clearly indicated that ibrutinib inhibited both BTK and STAT3 activation in MCL cells, we next elucidated the function and action between BTK and STAT3. The results showed that transient knockdown of BTK significantly inhibited STAT3 phosphorylation in MCL cells. Next, the results from both immunoprecipitation and confocal microscopy showed that STAT3 was BTK-associated transcription protein indicating that BTK could function as a kinase upstream of STAT3, in a similar manner to the JAK/STAT pathway. Since STAT3 is predominately known as the downstream protein of the IL-6/JAK pathway, we examined whether there is a cross-talk between the BTK-STAT3 and the JAK-STAT3 pathways in MCL cells. After stimulation of MCL cells with IgM or IL-6, ibrutinib only inhibited IgM-induced STAT3 activation but not IL-6-induced STAT3 activation. Even with an increased dose of ibrutinib, the basal level of STAT3 phosphorylation remains detectable in MCL cells due to IL-6 autocrine. However, ibrutinib plus JAK inhibitor completely inactivated STAT3 and synergistically inhibited the growth of MCL cells. These data indicate that there are two independent pathways, BCR-BTK and IL6-JAK, which lead to STAT3 activation without cross-talk in MCL cells.

Our results may lead to the development of more effective combination therapy to block both BCR-BTK and IL-6-JAK signaling pathways for relapsed or refractory MCL.

publications.title: Potent Inhibition of the Growth and Induction of Apoptosis of Mantle Cell Lymphoma By the Novel Anthracycline Berubicin in Vitro and in Vivo
publications.description:
Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is a distinct, aggressive, and heterogeneous subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) that has a median failure-free survival duration of 12 to 16 months after anthracycline-based therapy. Rituximab in combination with hyperfractionated cyclophosphamide, vincristine, doxorubicin (DOX), and dexamethasone (R-hyperCVAD) has been a successful frontline therapy for MCL, with complete remission rates as high as 87% in patients. However, the efficacy of R-hyperCVAD comes at the expense of severe grade III-IV toxicities, and its use is limited by de novo or acquired multidrug resistance. Thus, efforts must be made to update the agents in this regimen. 

Berubicin (WP744; BRN) is a clinically evaluated, 4’-O-benzylated analog of DOX that, like DOX, stabilizes cleavable complexes between DNA and topoisomerase II, leading to irreversible double-strand DNA breaks and abrogation of DNA religation. In contrast to DOX, BRN overcomes multidrug resistance by circumventing efflux mediated by ATP-binding cassette proteins like P-glycoprotein and MRP-1. BRN is also the first anthracycline derivative to effectively cross the blood-brain barrier, with demonstrated phase 1 responses in brain cancer patients. In this study, we investigated the effect on BRN on growth inhibition and cell cycle alterations in MCL cell lines in vitro. We also assessed BRN’s efficacy in vivo in MCL-bearing SCID/SCID-hu mice.

publications.title: Anti-CD20 and B-Cell Receptor-Mediated Growth Inhibition and Apoptosis: A Preclinical Study of Ibrutinib and Rituximab Combination Therapy in Mantle Cell Lymphoma in Vitro and in Vivo(Link)
publications.description:
Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is an aggressive B-cell lymphoma with poor outcome and therapeutic challenge. Oral single-agent ibrutinib, a Bruton’s tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor, elicited a response rate of 68% in phase II clinical trial and has been approved by FDA for the treatment of MCL patients who received at least one prior therapy. To increase the response rate, the combination of ibrutinib with rituximab would be an ideal regimen because: (1) Both BTK and CD20 are effective therapeutic targets for MCL; (2) CD20-dependent apoptosis occurs associated with B-cell receptor (BCR) activity. Regardless rituximab-mediated immune response (ADCC and CDC) and ibrutinib-mediated ITK inhibition (Th1 polarization), an important potential effect of ibrutinib and rituximab may enhance the direct anti-MCL cytotoxicity of the combination. 

Based on our preclinical data of rituximab and ibrutinib combination in vitro and in primary MCL-bearing SCID-hu mice, ibrutinib plus rituximab could be an effective regimen in a clinical trial of relapsed or refractory MCL

I was a 2020 Disability Lead Fellow and a 2021 New Leaders Council Fellow. I graduated with honors from UChicago with a bachelor’s degree in Psychology and Public Policy.

In my free time, I'm usually listening to a policy podcast, challenging myself in pilates, or facetiming with my adopted cat – not necessarily in that order.

honorsAndAwards.description: "This award is in recognition of Allison's significant contribution on a challenging client engagement. Since it was a very large data deliverable, it took several rounds of QCing to ensure it was exactly what the client was looking for, and Allison performed the task for each delivery. Our client was not familiar with our methodology and had many questions about the data in which Allison was always willing to jump in and respond. Allison made herself available to chat live with the client and answer specific questions on the data pull. In several cases the client manipulated the data incorrectly and was questioning the accuracy of our data. Allison was professional and provided responses to help troubleshoot the issues they were having. Each time, Allison had provided a solution to the client, which showcased the accuracy of Nielsen’s data and the excellent service our analysts provide to ensure the client has a full understanding of what they are analyzing.  Allison created a playbook in which she captured the client’s feedback throughout the engagement to ensure moving forward we are able to replicate the deliverable in a similar manner each time.  Thanks to Allison for her hard work, dedication and professionalism in dealing with a challenging client!!   We were able to renew the agreement thru December 2016!"

publications.title: Regulation of Next Generation Networks: Structural Separation, Access Regulation, or No Regulation at All?
publications.description:
Since the introduction of Next Generation Networks (NGNs) by
telecommunication network operators, national regulators have begun to adapt their
access regulation regimes to the new technological conditions. The regulatory reactions
gravitate towards three distinct regulatory trajectories: unregulated competition, access
regulation, and structural separation. We first analyze the extent of market power in
access Networks in NGNs from a technological perspective. Second, we use case studies
to identify patterns between technological and market conditions and regulators' reactions
in selected countries. We find that market power in the access network is likely to prevail.
Regulatory reactions differ with the extent of infrastructure competition and the regulators
position in the trade-off between promoting investment and protecting competition

publications.title: Context-Aware Multimedia Provisioning for Pervasive Game
publications.publishedAt: Proceedings of 7th IEEE Symposium on Multimedia · Dec 12, 2005
publications.description: Pervasive gaming, mobile gaming applications interleaved into the real world, is an emerging field for context-aware multimedia applications. Mobile multimedia applications are fostered by the improvement of hardware technology and the emergence of new devices with sufficient networking and processing capabilities. However, these extending possibilities also increase the complexity of software development due to the distributed mobile environment. This paper presents a framework enabling rapid development and easy deployment of scalable, context-aware multimedia applications for mobile environments. Subsequently, the development of "Cron", a pervasive game operating in the city area of Berlin, Germany, is introduced to prove the framework concept and demonstrate its features as well as potential for further research.

publications.description:
Our Snapshot series began in March 2020 and includes more than twenty articles and slideshows delivered periodically over the ensuing 18 months. The series tracks sentiment and spending changes due to COVID-19.

The series is based on data drawn from an online survey of consumers that has been conducted regularly since early March 2020 across multiple countries worldwide. Each Snapshot highlights a selection of insights from a comprehensive ongoing study that BCG provides to clients. The survey is produced by the authors, who are members of BCG’s Center for Customer Insight (CCI), in partnership with coding and sampling provider Dynata, the world’s largest first-party data and insights platform. The goal of the research is to provide our clients and businesses around the world with periodic barometer readings of COVID-19-related consumer sentiment and actual and anticipated consumer behavior and spending to inform critical crisis triage activities, as well as rebound planning and decision making.

publications.title: Unlocking acquisitive growth - Lessons from serial acquirors
publications.description: Successful serial acquirers deliver more growth and create more value from acquisitions than their peers. What explains their success? A willingness to invest disproportionately in three key areas: defining a compelling investment thesis, building an enduring M&A network and culture, and establishing distinctive principles to guide the M&A process.

publications.title: Do It Yourself Activism
publications.description: Senior managers and the board can borrow directly from the activist’s playbook by critically examining their company’s portfolio, balance sheet, and governance in much the same way that an activist investor would, and then preemptively making necessary changes. By engaging in what we call do-it-yourself activism, senior management can make a company less attractive to activists by making it more attractive to long-term shareholders.

publications.title: Improving the odds:  Strategies for superior value creation
publications.description: The report offers four different perspectives on successful value creation. We begin by exploring how companies can chart a course toward superior value creation in today’s low-growth economic environment. Next, we introduce some new BCG research on the theme of value patterns, distinctive company starting positions that cut across industry boundaries and shape the range and types of strategic moves most likely to create value. We follow with a detailed case study of how one BCG client, the consumer-packaged-goods company Church & Dwight, has delivered superior shareholder value—with an emphasis on the nuts and bolts of making it happen. Finally, we conclude with our annual rankings of the top ten value creators worldwide and in 21 industries for the five-year period from 2007 through 2011.

publications.title: How Value Patterns Work
publications.description: Although each company’s context is unique, there are recurring common patterns that show similar performance priorities, tradeoffs, and risks. BCG has been exploring how to quantify these patterns. In-depth discussions with professional investors, detailed company vignettes, and a statistical clustering of 2,700 global companies have led us to identify ten different value patterns, or company starting points, that cut across industry boundaries and shape the range and types of strategic moves that are most likely to create value. To illustrate how these value patterns work, let’s look in detail at one of the larger groups: high-value brands.

publications.title: Value Patterns:  The Concept
publications.description:
A value pattern describes how a company’s starting position shapes the strategic moves most likely to create value.  BCG has identified ten value patterns, each with its own distinctive combination of opportunities, tradeoffs, risks, and strategic moves.

Value patterns cut across industry boundaries and have distinct drivers of valuation multiples.  Value patterns offer a fresh lens for aligning corporate priorities with the moves that will create advantage and value.

publications.title: Succeeding in Uncertain Times
publications.description: The latest in our Collateral Damage series reviews recent BCG research on companies that have managed to drive sustained growth during the most recent downturn.  The research shows three types of growth companies:  pure-play category innovators, global challengers, and companies that have repositioned for growth.  Despite their wide-ranging profiles, these successful growing companies have common strategic themes:  strategic focus on a small number of significant opportunities;  meaningful innovation targeted at creating value for end-customers;  and consistent leadership choices to encourage a culture of speed and experimentation.

publications.title: The CEO as Investor
publications.description: Many strategic choices are investment choices.  By developing an explicit corporate investment thesis, much as professional investors do, leaders can do a better job making relevant bets and managing downside risks.  Different companies will need to focus on different areas to create value – company starting positions are multidimensional and inform investment priorities.

experience.description:
Due to a business acquisition, I joined Tekni-Plex Flexibles Healthcare Packaging as the sole Process Engineer for the facility. Tekni-Plex Madison manufactures flexible packaging for customers in the medical industry. The facility's web converting processes include flexographic printing, gravure coating, air knife coating, and extrusion laminating.

My key responsibilities included:

• Planned and implemented capital projects, including vision systems, trim and scrap handling equipment, and press repairs
• Managed Installation and Operational Qualification (IQ/OQ) of 2 roll slitters and 1 roll editor
• Coordinated external prepress services and plate manufacturing for flexographic printing
• Led production trials and process improvements

experience.companyName: Amcor Flexibles Europe, Middle East & Africa / Amcor Flexibles Americas
experience.description:
Amcor Flexibles Madison produces flexible packaging for Food and Home & Personal Care customers. The facility also produced Medical packaging. The facility's web converting processes included gravure printing and coating, adhesive lamination, flexographic printing, air knife coating, and extrusion lamination. In June 2019, Amcor sold the Medical business and assets to Tekni-Plex, Inc.

As a Process Engineer I focused on production, continuous improvement, and capital projects. Highlights of my accomplishments in this role:

• Created a Process Specifications Database using VBA for gravure press, adhesive laminator, and extrusion laminator line specifications by product
• Coordinated transition from internal to external manufacturing of flexographic plates
• Managed validation of process changes, such as changes in raw material supplier, to ensure product quality and safety
• Developed Installation and Operational Qualification (IQ/OQ) plan for new triplex adhesive laminator
• Led Sustainability Committee to increase production waste recycling and energy recovery rates
• Established the Amcor Madison Technical Women's Network and hosted monthly professional development events

As a Process Automation Engineer for Dow Technical Expertise and Support (TES), I supported Ion Exchange (IX) Resins at the Michigan Operations site. IX resins serve a variety of industries, including food & beverage, mining, water treatment, and microelectronics.

A highlight of my work was converting the control system for an aminator reactor from Dow MOD 5 to ABB 800xA. My other projects focused on improving process safety by implementing Safety Instrumented Systems (SIS) and updating control programming for capital projects. Additionally, I served as the TES Sustainability Team Leader, coordinating the department recycling program and organizing events to promote sustainability.

As a summer intern at the Dow Chemical Company, I supported Dow Automotive Systems at the Michigan Operations manufacturing site. The facility produced BETAMATE™ structural adhesives, used to replace welds and mechanical fasteners to improve vehicle durability while reducing weight and manufacturing cost. The facility is also one of the largest global producers of brake fluids.

Highlights of my achievements:

I managed 5S projects to organize 3 areas of the Structural Adhesives and Brake Fluids manufacturing buildings, working with a team of operators and maintenance coordinators. I performed air emissions calculations for obtaining a flexible air emissions permit from the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality to enable expansion of production. I analyzed Dow Automotive assets and capabilities and created presentation for soliciting external business use of facilities.

I had 2 back-to-back co-op terms at Kimberly-Clark Corporation Research & Engineering. I worked in the Baby & Child Care (BCC) Life Cycle Maximization (LCM) team, focused on extending the life of manufacturing lines for Huggies® and Pull-Ups® and reducing production waste. As part of my work, I traveled several times to manufacturing plants in Paris, Texas, and Ogden, Utah.

Highlights of my achievements:

I hosted a Kaizen event that identified root cause and implemented corrective actions to solve a $40,000/year machine tension problem. As the process engineering lead for a $1MM capital project, I created process set-up and quality protocol documents to reduce raw material waste on U.S. diaper machines. I analyzed process data in JMP to drive productivity and reduce waste, and implemented a new method of measuring and tracking waste at the core of raw material rolls. Additionally, I served as Website Chair for the Co-op and Intern Network's Harbor House Annual Golf Outing that raised $10,000 toward support and refuge for domestic abuse survivors.

I worked in the lab of Dr. Michael Plewa. The focus of our research was assessing the cytotoxicity of disinfection by-products (DBPs) in drinking water generated from different disinfection processes, to understand the impacts on human health and the environment. I maintained microbiology lab equipment, prepared and plated the Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells, and performed tests. 

The WaterCAMPWS Program for Undergraduate Research Experience (PURE) program included professional development workshops. I developed skills in scientific writing, project management, and poster and presentation design. I concluded the REU by presenting at a symposium and presenting a poster at the 2012 Illinois Water Conference Student Poster Session.

publications.title: Rapid Seeding of Blood-Derived Endothelial Cells onto Sintered Titanium for Ventricular Assist Device Application Creates Antithrombotic Coating
publications.publishedAt: American Society for Artificial Internal Organs Journal · Jan 20, 2016
publications.description: The most promising alternatives to heart transplantation are left ventricular assist devices and artificial hearts; however their use has been limited by thrombotic complications. To reduce these, sintered titanium (Ti) surfaces were developed, but thrombosis still occurs in ~7.5% of patients. We have invented a rapid-seeding technology to minimize the risk of thrombosis by rapid endothelialization of sintered Ti with human cord blood-derived endothelial cells (hCB-ECs). hCB-ECs were seeded within minutes onto sintered Ti and exposed to thrombosis-prone low fluid flow shear stresses. The hCB-ECs adhered and formed a confluent endothelial monolayer on sintered Ti. The exposure of sintered Ti to 4.4 dynes/cm for 20 hr immediately following rapid-seeding resulted in ~70% cell adherence. The cell adherence was not significantly increased by additional ex vivo static culture of rapid-seeded sintered Ti prior to flow exposure. In addition, adherent hCB-ECs remained functional on sintered Ti, as indicated by flow-induced increase in nitric oxide secretion and reduction in platelet adhesion. After 15-day ex vivo static culture, the adherent hCB-ECs remained metabolically active, expressed EC functional marker thrombomodulin, and reduced platelet adhesion. In conclusion, our results demonstrate the feasibility of rapid-seeding sintered Ti with blood-derived hCB-ECs to generate a living antithrombotic surface.

headline: Partner at BCG | Large-Scale Transformation, Change Management, Corporate Strategy, Value Creation
about:
As a Partner at BCG in Chicago, Chris Trakimas helps organizations address their most complex challenges, lead large-scale transformations, and unlock sustainable long-term value. He works across industries, integrating strategic advisory with hands-on operational experience to design solutions that are ambitious, pragmatic, and built to scale.

Chris focuses on corporate strategy, Transformation, and value creation. He partners closely with executive teams to define strategic priorities, accelerate performance, and drive cross-functional change across global organizations. Known for turning strategy into measurable impact, he thrives on solving difficult business problems and delivering outcomes that matter.

Chris began his career at GE in corporate finance and strategy, where he led financial, operational, and strategic improvement initiatives worldwide. This foundation shapes his approach today—bringing together the top-down perspective of a strategist with the executional mindset of an operator.

Beyond client work, Chris is deeply committed to leadership development and mentorship. He actively coaches emerging leaders and invests in building high-performing, values-driven teams. He is energized by collaborating with people who challenge convention and strive to expand the boundaries of innovation and impact.

Seasoned Product Manager specialising in the fintech sector, with a rich educational background including an MBA from London Business School and international experience from Chicago Booth School of Business.

Throughout my career, I've focused on bridging the gap between finance and technology, spearheading initiatives that optimise financial operations and enhance customer engagement through data-driven insights and innovative solutions. My work at top-tier consulting companies and financial institutions has enabled me to lead significant projects, from developing state-of-the-art trading and CRM platforms using microservices architecture to implementing strategic API integrations that support hundreds of thousands of clients. I also hold Certified Financial Analyst (CFA) and Financial Risk Manager (FRM) qualifications that underpin my strategic decision-making and risk management capabilities.

Leadership is at the core of my professional ethos. I've managed diverse teams, fostering an environment of innovation and accountability, and driven projects that not only meet but anticipate market needs and challenges. My goal is to continue leveraging my expertise to lead fintech solutions that are not only technologically advanced but also strategically aligned with global financial trends and customer needs.

I am passionate about the transformative power of fintech and am always open to connecting with like-minded professionals and exploring new opportunities to innovate within this exciting field.

I'm passionate about driving sustainable innovation and helping global organizations tackle the challenges of decarbonization. At Boston Consulting Group (BCG), I collaborate with leading companies—particularly in hard-to-abate sectors like aluminum, steel, and cement—to adopt cutting-edge, low-carbon technologies and set new industry standards in sustainability.

With a Master’s in Sustainability and Social Innovation from HEC Paris, I combine deep academic knowledge with hands-on experience in developing strategies that deliver tangible results. From leading decarbonization efforts in industrial sectors to building emissions abatement strategies for global consumer brands, my work consistently focuses on measurable outcomes that accelerate the path to net-zero.

I’m driven by the belief that overcoming the complex challenges of climate change requires bold collaboration and innovation across industries. My mission is to help organizations make a lasting, positive impact on the global climate by driving forward transformative solutions that pave the way for a more sustainable and resilient future.

publications.description:
For higher education institutions, the question is no longer whether change is needed, but how fast can institutions make it happen. 
Colleges and universities are facing an existential crisis due to converging pressures from lower enrollments, federal cuts, the emergence of AI, and changing societal expectations.
Fortunately, higher education leaders have an arsenal of powerful levers—technology, agile operational models, and valuable intellectual and brand assets—that can be activated for short-, medium-, and long-term gains.
Institutions that accelerate investment in digital infrastructure, workforce-relevant programming, deeper industry partnerships, and scalable revenue streams can not only safeguard their financial sustainability but also build more resilient, future-ready organizations.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Professor of Bioinformatics at Brigham Young University
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: February 12, 2015, Perry was Dane’s teacher
receivedRecommendations.description: I met Dane when he was a student in a course I taught: Introduction to Bioinformatics. This course consists of two main components. The first component is a survey of the bioinformatics field. Students are exposed to scientists from many different disciplines (e.g. human genetics, phylogenetics and systematics, botany, developmental biology, etc.) who are bioinformaticists themselves, or whose research would benefit from the use of bioinformatics and computational biology. Students are asked, specifically, to identify ways that bioinformatics could improve their ability to test scientific hypotheses in the labs they work in. In the second component of the class students learn to use regular expressions and are introduced to the Python programming language. This is a very rigorous class and the majority of the students have no prior programming experience; however, they are expected to learn quickly and by the end of the semester students who succeed are able to perform simple manipulations of large VCF files (files used for storing genetic information from next-generation sequencing projects). Dane worked very hard and consistently improved. He demonstrated that he is capable of quickly learning very difficult concepts. I happily recommend Dane and am confident he will be successful in whatever he chooses.

about:
I'm a motivated graduate student at Princeton University's Molecular Biology Department. Throughout my thesis project, I worked as a graduate student in Professor Coleen Murphy's lab, where I studied the cognitive aging process using wild-type and long-lived C. elegans models, applying genetic, genomic, and behavioral methods to characterize the aging process and identify pro-longevity genes and pathways in neurons that are conserved from worm to human. 
During this time, I demonstrated my motivation, hard work, scientific insight, experimental skills, and data analysis and programming skills. I gained valuable experience in problem-solving, collaboration, critical thinking, and research experience in model organisms, behavioral paradigms, and bulk and single-nucleus RNA sequencing. My thesis works resulted in 3 first author and co-first-author papers currently in submission to top journals. 
Prior to arriving at Princeton, I studied at Peking University, where I obtained a B.S. in Biological sciences. I worked on neurodegenerative diseases in mouse models, and I also completed a summer research program at the University of Chicago, where I worked on motor neuron terminal differentiation.

publications.title: Male-specific behavioral and transcriptomic changes in aging C. elegans neurons
publications.description:
•Male worms undergo cognitive decline and neuron morphology defects with age
•Male neuron RNA-seq uncovers sexual dimorphism in transcriptomic changes with age
•X chromosome genes have a greater hermaphrodite bias with age
•hrg-7, whose expression declines with age, is required for male sensory behaviors

publications.title: The Neuron-specific IIS/FOXO Transcriptome in Aged Animals Reveals Regulatory Mechanisms of Cognitive Aging
publications.description: Cognitive decline is a significant health concern in our aging society. Here, we used the model organism C. elegans to investigate the impact of the IIS/FOXO pathway on age-related cognitive decline. The daf-2 Insulin/IGF-1 receptor mutant exhibits a significant extension of learning and memory span with age compared to wild-type worms, an effect that is dependent on the DAF-16 transcription factor. To identify possible mechanisms by which aging daf-2 mutants maintain learning and memory with age while wild-type worms lose neuronal function, we carried out neuron-specific transcriptomic analysis in aged animals. We observed downregulation of neuronal genes and upregulation of transcriptional regulation genes in aging wild-type neurons. By contrast, IIS/FOXO pathway mutants exhibit distinct neuronal transcriptomic alterations in response to cognitive aging, including upregulation of stress response genes and downregulation of specific insulin signaling genes. We tested the roles of significantly transcriptionally-changed genes in regulating cognitive functions, identifying novel regulators of learning and memory. In addition to other mechanistic insights, comparison of the aged vs young daf-2 neuronal transcriptome revealed that a new set of potentially neuroprotective genes is upregulated; instead of simply mimicking a young state, daf-2 may enhance neuronal resilience to accumulation of harm and take a more active approach to combat aging. These findings suggest a potential mechanism for regulating cognitive function with age and offer insights into novel therapeutic targets for age-related cognitive decline.

publications.title: Adult Single-nucleus Neuronal Transcriptomes of Insulin Signaling Mutants Reveal Regulators of Behavior and Learning
publications.description: The insulin/insulin-like signaling (IIS) pathway regulates many of C. elegans′ adult functions, including learning and memory1. While whole-worm and tissue-specific transcriptomic analyses have identified IIS targets2,3, a higher-resolution single-cell approach is required to identify changes that confer neuron-specific improvements in the long-lived insulin receptor mutant, daf-2. To understand how behaviors that are controlled by a small number of neurons change in daf-2 mutants, we used the deep resolution of single-nucleus RNA sequencing to define each neuron type′s transcriptome in adult wild-type and daf-2 mutants. First, we found surprising differences between wild-type L4 larval neurons and young adult neurons in chemoreceptor expression, synaptic genes, and learning and memory genes. These Day 1 adult neuron transcriptomes allowed us to identify adult AWC-specific regulators of chemosensory function and to predict neuron-to-neuron peptide/receptor pairs. We then identified gene expression changes that correlate with daf-2′s improved cognitive functions, particularly in the AWC sensory neuron that controls learning and associative memory4, and used behavioral assays to test their roles in cognitive function. Combining deep single-neuron transcriptomics, genetic manipulation, and behavioral analyses enabled us to identify genes that may function in a single adult neuron to control behavior, including conserved genes that function in learning and memory.

publications.title: Male-specific features of C. elegans neuronal aging
publications.description: Aging is a complex biological process, with sexually dimorphic aspects. For example, men and women differ in their vulnerabilities in cognitive decline, suggesting biological sex may contribute to the heterogeneous nature of aging. Although we know a great deal about the cognitive aging of hermaphrodites of the model system C. elegans, less is known about cognitive decline in males. Through behavioral analyses, we found that the cognitive aging process has both sex-shared and sex-dimorphic characteristics. Through neuron-specific sequencing, we identified neuronal age-associated sex-differential targets. In addition to sex-shared neuronal aging genes, males differentially downregulate mitochondrial metabolic genes and upregulate GPCR genes with age. In addition, the X chromosome exhibits increased gene expression in hermaphrodites and altered dosage compensation complex expression with age, indicating possible X-chromosomal dysregulation that contributes to sexual dimorphism in cognitive aging. Finally, we found that the sex-differentially expressed gene hrg-7, which encodes an aspartic-type endopeptidase, regulates male behavior during cognitive aging but does not affect hermaphrodites’ behaviors. Overall, these results suggest that males and hermaphrodites exhibit different age-related neuronal changes. This study will strengthen our understanding of sex-specific vulnerability and resilience and help identify new pathways to target with novel treatments that could benefit both sexes.

publications.title: Neuronal activation of Gaq EGL-30/GNAQ late in life rejuvenates cognition across species
publications.description: Loss of cognitive function with age is devastating. EGL-30/GNAQ and Gaq signaling pathways are highly conserved between C. elegans and mammals, and murine Gnaq is enriched in hippocampal neurons and de- clines with age. We found that activation of EGL-30 in aged worms triples memory span, and GNAQ gain of function significantly improved memory in aged mice: GNAQ(gf) in hippocampal neurons of 24-month-old mice (equivalent to 70- to 80-year-old humans) rescued age-related impairments in well-being and memory. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed increased expression of genes regulating synaptic function, axon guidance, and memory in GNAQ-treated mice, and worm orthologs of these genes were required for long- term memory extension in worms. These experiments demonstrate that C. elegans is a powerful model to identify mammalian regulators of memory, leading to the identification of a pathway that improves memory in extremely old mice. To our knowledge, this is the oldest age at which an intervention has improved age- related cognitive decline.

Here, we used the model organism C. elegans to investigate the impact of the IIS/FOXO pathway on age-related cognitive decline. The daf-2 Insulin/IGF-1 receptor mutant exhibits a significant extension of learning and memory span with age compared to wild-type worms, an effect that is dependent on the DAF-16 transcription factor. To identify possible mechanisms by which aging daf-2 mutants maintain learning and memory with age while wild-type worms lose neuronal function, we carried out neuron-specific transcriptomic analysis in aged animals. We observed downregulation of neuronal genes and upregulation of transcriptional regulation genes in aging wild-type neurons. By contrast, IIS/FOXO pathway mutants exhibit distinct neuronal transcriptomic alterations in response to cognitive aging, including upregulation of stress response genes and downregulation of specific insulin signaling genes. We tested the roles of significantly transcriptionally-changed genes in regulating cognitive functions, identifying novel regulators of learning and memory. In addition to other mechanistic insights, comparison of the aged vs young daf-2 neuronal transcriptome revealed that a new set of potentially neuroprotective genes is upregulated; instead of simply mimicking a young state, daf-2 may enhance neuronal resilience to accumulation of harm and take a more active approach to combat aging. These findings suggest a potential mechanism for regulating cognitive function with age and offer insights into novel therapeutic targets for age-related cognitive decline.

publications.title: Control of spinal motor neuron terminal differentiation through sustained Hoxc8 gene activity
publications.description: Spinal motor neurons (MNs) constitute cellular substrates for several movement disorders. Although their early development has received much attention, how spinal MNs become and remain terminally differentiated is poorly understood. Here, we determined the transcriptome of mouse MNs located at the brachial domain of the spinal cord at embryonic and postnatal stages. We identified novel transcription factors (TFs) and terminal differentiation genes (e.g. ion channels, neurotransmitter receptors, adhesion molecules) with continuous expression in MNs. Interestingly, genes encoding homeodomain TFs (e.g. HOX, LIM), previously implicated in early MN development, continue to be expressed postnatally, suggesting later functions. To test this idea, we inactivated Hoxc8 at successive stages of mouse MN development and observed motor deficits. Our in vivo findings suggest that Hoxc8 is not only required to establish, but also maintain expression of several MN terminal differentiation markers. Data from in vitro generated MNs indicate Hoxc8 acts directly and is sufficient to induce expression of terminal differentiation genes. Our findings dovetail recent observations in Caenorhabditis elegans MNs, pointing toward an evolutionarily conserved role for Hox in neuronal terminal differentiation.

headline: Senior Advisor at The Boston Consulting Group (BCG)
about:
I am a globally recognized senior Information Technology expert and consultant. Following nearly forty years of experience creating and delivering solutions to clients around the world and leadership of global technology practices with Accenture, Boston Consulting Group and American Management Systems, I have retired from Accenture and am in private practice advising senior IT and business executives and Boards of Directors.

With a focus on financial services and global capital markets, I have served most of the world’s major broker-dealers and many equities and fixed-income exchanges, universal banks, private equity funds, hedge funds and global payment networks. Examples of my recent experience include leading:

- Development and implementation of global IT operating models for US and European universal banks. 
- Development of strategies to improve IT’s cost effectiveness and business enablement.
- Independent forensic analysis of adverse “events” in global exchange trading and global payments processing, including testimony before national regulatory bodies.
- Pre-acquisition due diligence for major transactions by private equity funds and global merchant banks with career experience including more than seventy-five such transactions.
- Post-merger integration of IT and business operations following large, global transactions.
- Serving, at the request of the CIO, as interim Global CTO for one of Accenture’s largest financial services clients.

Examples of my current practice include:

- Advising CIOs and CTOs on IT strategy and transformation of the IT function’s costs and business effectiveness.
- Advising senior business executives on improving business performance via IT-enabling investments.
- Advising Boards of Directors on structuring to oversee IT performance and IT-related risk.
- Evaluation of proposed major IT initiatives.
- Forensic analysis of adverse IT “events”.
- Pre-acquisition technology-focused due diligence.

headline: Product Lead | Innovator and Business Builder
about:
I'm a product leader who loves building things—especially products that solve real problems and create tangible impact.

At BCG X, I partner closely with global clients and multidisciplinary teams to launch and scale digital ventures. That means diving into big, messy problems and turning them into clear strategies and products that customers actually want and use. I've built products from scratch, helped companies find their product-market fit, and scaled solutions across healthtech, fintech, consumer tech, and beyond.

My approach is collaborative and pragmatic. I believe great products come from empowered teams, clear communication, and a genuine curiosity to learn and adapt along the way. I'm at my best navigating ambiguity, aligning diverse stakeholders, and translating complex ideas into practical, actionable plans.

I'm always interested in meeting thoughtful people, learning something new, and talking about what's next in tech, strategy, or just the best new coffee spot. Feel free to reach out!

publications.title: Missionaries Outperform in Venture Funding
publications.publishedAt: International Journal of Entrepreneurship, Vol.26 Iss.5 · Sep 1, 2022
publications.description:
Scientific paper about the impact of founder characteristics and motives on funding performance of new ventures (total amount of funding raised / number of funding rounds closed). Key finding: Founders motivated by the desire to contribute to society & a multi-stakeholder approach (Missionary founder social identity) are more successful in raising funds than those being motivated by economic goals only.


ABSTRACT

While prior research has evidenced the impact of founder social identities on new venture creation, our understanding of how founder identity affects funding performance as a critical determinant for venture success is limited. Given that different identities define various motivational concepts—that is, missionaries increasing benefits for society at large, as opposed to darwinians maximizing economic self-interest and communitarians supporting a particular community—we propose a model for how such founder identity differences relate to ambiguous funding outcomes. 
Our findings reveal that the missionary founder social identity has a significantly positive impact on funding performance. 
We discuss our contributions to founder social identity theory and its intersection with behavioral finance.

headline: Consultant | MBA | Change Management | Organisational Development
about:
I’m am an MBA candidate at Chicago Booth looking to pursue a career in change management and organisational development. I believe the work I do not only supports the current business needs and strategy but also the people, who are instrumental to any organisation's long term success. I am fascinated about behaviour, intrinsic motivation and how people manage change. I love reading about these topics and using my Psychology degree to bring them into my work. I am also interested in how collecting feedback and data can help strengthen and further improve engagement and performance.

I remain deeply curious about the world around me, and this has manifested itself in my career. Having moved internationally multiple times, and by working in a global company and understanding the importance of bringing cultures together, I continue to develop my language skills. I chose an international firm, to gain experience of company culture across regions and in over 40 offices. This has enabled me to build relationships with people of all seniority, speak different languages, and improve my analytical skills through the different projects that I manage. 

In my personal life I enjoy playing tennis, skiing with my family and experimenting in the kitchen. I am the eldest of 4 and believe this has provided me with resilience, leadership and an open-mindset.

If you would like to find out more about me, please contact me on LinkedIn or at jesskiva@gmail.com

Why the First Year Matters for LGBTQ+ Employees
publications.description: The first year of employment is critical for LGBTQ+ employees, with 70% coming out then or likely not at all. This has major implications for companies, as employees who feel comfortable sharing their identity at work report feeling more empowered, more comfortable about speaking up, being themselves, and building close friendships at work. Our survey of ~ 8,800 people in 19 countries also shed light on the challenges that trans and gender nonconforming (TGNC) employees and LBTQ+ women face when making choices about being out at work. For instance, 74% of TGNC respondents reported instances of discrimination versus 57% of LGBQ+ respondents. And LBTQ+ women who are out reported a 13% greater incidence of sexual harassment than did their male counterparts. The article outlines 5 concrete areas, across the employee lifecycle, that companies can address to encourage employees to be out.

headline: Senior Global Health Expert | Ecosystem Catalyst | Problem Solver | Board Chair |
topSkills: Strategic Planning • Analysis • Program Evaluation • Research • Program Management
about:
With over 17 years of experience covering all aspects of Global Health, I am a PPL at Boston Consulting Group (BCG), where I apply my expertise in global and public health, universal health coverage, primary healthcare, and community health systems to solve complex challenges and create social impact. I  hold an MA in International Development & Policy from the University of Chicago, an MBA from MIT, an MPA from Harvard Kennedy School, and undergraduate degrees from the University of Pennsylvania.

I have served as Senior Advisor to Cabinet Ministers in multiple governments to advance their ambitious strategic health plans. In Kenya, I was Senior Advisor to the Cabinet Secretary for Health working with with the Office of the President on Universal Health Coverage advancing to the President's Big 4 Agenda. 

Tapping into the entrepreneurial ecosystems at MIT and Harvard; I am an Advisor at HER Heard, a start-up that amplifies the voices of women, and a founder of This Generation Now and the African Century VC-Impact Fund, two initiatives that aim to empower and mobilize young African leaders and innovators in the health sector.

As a clinician, an entrepreneur, a private and VC investor, a high-impact consultant, and a board chair, I have a multidimensional perspective and a passion for driving positive change in the health sector and beyond. I have worked with diverse stakeholders, including governments, nonprofits, and private sector partners, to design and implement innovative solutions and strategies that improve health outcomes and access in Africa and other regions.

All-in-all, I have raised and deployed nearly $1 billion from multi-laterals, foundations, and governments to other governments and programs so that they can strengthen public health systems, reach marginalized communities, and enhance life-saving access for tens of millions.
